issue.title: Claude subscription bridge: a deferred client MCP tool fails on its own name, works as mcp__magpie__<name>
issue.body:
**Version:** magpie 0.1.2627, gateway on macOS, Claude Code 2.1.316, served by a saved Claude account (setup-token) through the subscription bridge. I read `bridgeToolName` on current `main` and the branch below is unchanged there, but I have not rerun this on a newer build.

**What happens**

A deferred MCP tool from one of the client's own servers can't be called by the name the client gives it. After ToolSearch loads it, the model calls the name it was told and the run answers `No such tool available`. The model then retries with `mcp__magpie__<client name>`, which works.

With a read-only stock lookup from the client's `yfinance` MCP server:

1. ToolSearch: `select:mcp__yfinance__get_stock_info`
2. Model calls `mcp__yfinance__get_stock_info`: `No such tool available`
3. Model calls `mcp__magpie__mcp__yfinance__get_stock_info`: works

This happened in 6 of 6 new sessions (3 on `claude-opus-5-5`, 3 on `claude-sonnet-5-5`), run with `claude -p ... --dangerously-skip-permissions`. The prompt asked the model to report its first and second tool names, so the failed first call comes from the model's own report. The client's stream only shows the one successful `tool_use`. Built-in tools such as Bash, Read, Skill and Agent didn't show this in the same sessions.

**Why I think it happens**

`bridgeToolName` removes the helper's prefix only for names that start with `mcp__magpie__`, the fix for the double prefix on magpie's own Library tools (packinggoods, 11-01). Its comment notes that a deferred tool the client named in its text kept the single prefix. Any other client MCP tool, such as `mcp__yfinance__x`, is still offered as `mcp__magpie__mcp__yfinance__x`, while the client's text and ToolSearch result call it `mcp__yfinance__x`, so the two names differ.

**Impact**

Each session costs one extra failed call per deferred MCP tool, and a less persistent model could give up and report the tool as missing. It also adds a turn that the client can't see.

**Expected**

The name the client uses for a tool works on the first call. Either the run offers the tool under the client's name, or the run's model is told the mapping.

I searched the issues for `mcp__magpie__mcp__`, `No such tool available` and tool-name prefixes and found no report of this. #2649 and #4610 are nearby but cover other problems.

comments.body:
Reproduced and fixed on a branch — your diagnosis was exactly right, and this is the one fix the maintainer's #4956 comment asks for over both issues: hand the client's own `mcp__<server>__…` names to the client.

**Root cause** (as you read it). After ToolSearch loads a deferred tool, the bridge offers it to the inner Claude Code as `mcp__magpie__mcp__yfinance__get_stock_info`, while the conversation — the client's ToolSearch result — calls it `mcp__yfinance__get_stock_info`. The model calls the name it was told; `toolStart` sees no `mcp__magpie__` prefix, treats the call as the inner run's own, and the inner Claude Code answers "No such tool available" on a turn the client never sees. The retry under the helper's full name maps back and works.

**Fix** (branch `fix/4956-4854-bridge-deferred-tool-names`, commit `3086a4960`, on top of main `8abdf53a8`):

- `toolStart` hands a no-prefix call to the client under the name the model called — the client's own — when that name is one the client said: a tool it sent in `tools` (`subscriptionRun.tools`, plus `clientMCPTools`, which folds the request's own `mcp__…` tool names into the run's `announced` map), or one its conversation announces (the deferred-tools reminder's `mcp__…` names, and the tools a result loads — #4956's unloaded half, fixed by the same commit).
- The run's own claude.ai connectors carry `mcp__…` names too and stay the run's own: a name the client neither sent nor announced is not handed over.

For your shape the tool is in the client's `tools` on the very turn the model first calls it, so **the name the client uses works on the first call** — no failed call, no extra hidden turn, which is the behavior your report asks for.

**Verification**:

| What | Result |
|---|---|
| The new bridge test on base (the one branch ablated) | red: `mcp__yfinance__get_stock_info` called by its own name hands the client nothing — the fake run answers its own call, exactly your step 2 |
| Same test on the branch | green in all five shapes: your loaded case, #4956's announced-unloaded case, the helper's full name mapping back to the declared one (your step 3, unchanged), a declared tool, and a connector's call kept the run's |
| Neighbors — the unloaded-magpie-tool test your report links to (packinggoods), magpie MCP names, structured output, `ToolName`/`ToolChoice` | ok |
| gofmt / `go vet -tags nogui` (linux, windows) / `go build -tags nogui` | clean |

**Boundary**: not run against your exact setup (Claude Code 2.1.316 with a real yfinance server); exercised through the same fake-run harness the maintainer reproduced packinggoods' report with, using the reminder wording from that capture. `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged` fails alone on clean main on this machine — pre-existing, unrelated.

This is a fork branch, offered for review; not a claim on the issue.

issue.title: Claude bridge: an unloaded deferred tool of another MCP server (mcp__linear__…) is answered by the run, not handed to the client

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Found while fixing packinggoods' report (#feedback 11-02, "调用mcp时总会提示错误然后重试成功").

In the Claude subscription bridge, the client's tools reach the inner Claude Code run through magpie's MCP helper (`mcp__magpie__<name>`). Claude Code with tool search on announces deferred MCP tools by name in a reminder and leaves them out of `tools` until `ToolSearch` loads them.

The fix for `mcp__magpie__…` tools hands such a call over under its full name (`toolStart` in `internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go`). A deferred tool of **another** client MCP server, e.g. `mcp__linear__get_issue`, is still not handed over: the inner model calls `mcp__linear__get_issue`, `toolStart` sees no `mcp__magpie__` prefix and treats it as the run's own call, and the inner Claude Code answers it "No MCP server provides it" itself. The client never sees the call; the model goes on without the tool, or loads it with ToolSearch and calls again.

Not changed in the same commit because a name without `mcp__magpie__` can also be one of the inner account's own claude.ai connectors, which the run must keep answering itself. A fix needs to tell the client's announced names apart (they are in the conversation's deferred-tools reminder) from the run's own.

issue.title: Claude subscription bridge: after a resume from a transcript, top-level tool calls reach the client still prefixed `mcp__magpie__` (client also has an MCP server named `magpie`)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**Environment**
- magpie 0.1.3749, Windows 11 (10.0.26300)
- Claude subscription bridge, auto mode. Bridged Claude Code 2.1.322 runs in `%TEMP%\magpie-claude-work` with `--tools ""`
- Client `~/.claude.json` has a single user-scope MCP server, named `magpie`: `{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:3425/mcp/magpie/hub/claude"}`

**Related, but not duplicates**
- #958: in that bug, a run started anew called the *bare* names. Its fix (e8a2b507, v0.1.1099) renders past calls as `[tool call mcp__magpie__X …]`. Here the model calls the *prefixed* names correctly, and the client receives them unconverted. This shows up only on that same resume-from-transcript path, so the #958 change may be involved.
- #5840: the alias is left unconverted for tool names *inside arguments*. Here it's the call's own top-level name.
- #4854: the name mismatch for deferred tools of *other* client MCP servers. Its body notes that `bridgeToolName` handles names that already start with `mcp__magpie__` as a special case (the fix for the double prefix on magpie's own Library tools, 11-01). That rule may be what's misfiring here; see the hypothesis below.
- #4804 / #4914: runs restarting or not being resumed. Possibly why a new run started on almost every turn after the resume.

**Expected:** when the model calls `mcp__magpie__PowerShell`, the client receives `PowerShell`, as it did before the resume.

**Actual:** after the resume, the client receives `mcp__magpie__PowerShell`. Claude Code sends that to its own `magpie` server (the hub), which has no such tool:

```
No such tool available: mcp__magpie__PowerShell. Its MCP server 'magpie' is connected but does not offer this tool here. Continue without it.
```

**Timeline** (local time, UTC−5)

| | Before (working) | After (failing) |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway conversation | `385d26e2…` | `ae339257…` |
| Client session | `5532dbdf` | `22f17099` |
| Window | 05:15–05:43 | 05:45:10 onward |
| Claude Code process | one long-lived process, pid 24940 | a new process on almost every turn (22420, 26804, 43080, …) |
| Tool names the client declared (gateway "Tools" context; magpie stores it cut short, so partial) | bare: `Agent`, `Artifact`, `AskUserQuestion`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep` | prefixed: `mcp__magpie__Agent`, `…Artifact`, `…AskUserQuestion`, `…Bash`, `…Edit`, `…Glob`, `…Grep`, `…ListAgents`, alongside bare `Agent` and `EndConversation` |
| tool_use names in gateway output | bare: `PowerShell` ×8, `Write` ×1 | prefixed: `mcp__magpie__PowerShell`, `…Bash`, `…Glob`, `…Read`, `…Grep`, `…ToolSearch` |
| Outcome | no errors; the `Write` at 05:39:35 created its file (confirmed on disk) | 20 failed calls across 7 bridged transcripts: PowerShell 7, Glob 4, Bash 3, Read 2, and one each for Agent, Grep, ListAgents and ToolSearch (counted once per `tool_use_id` from the transcripts' tool results; the gateway log doesn't record tool results) |

**app.log at the switch:**
```
05:43:16 claude: Claude Code pid 24940 (claude-opus-5-5) holds 438 MiB after its turn
05:45:13 claude: no run waits for this turn: no run here has had this conversation
05:45:13 claude: a new Claude Code goes on with the conversation from a transcript of it (25 messages, 0 images), typed the last turn's 2
05:45:13 claude: Claude Code pid 22420 started, a run on claude-opus-5-5 (interactive mode)
05:46:51 claude: Claude Code pid 26804 (claude-opus-5-5, interactive mode) ended after 2s (exit status 1)
05:46:51 gateway: claude's call to group/auto-claude-opus-5-5 on claude failed: 499 after 4.332s
```
app.log has no `tools/list` or schema errors in this window, which fits the failing calls never coming back to magpie.

**Possibly related**
- Between 05:40 and 05:44, several short `claude-haiku-5-5` runs ended with exit status 1 after 4–17 s, just before pid 24940 stopped being used.
- The tool list in the failing runs' `api-request-shape` (21 tools) has one extra entry, `mcp__magpie__EndConversation`, compared with an earlier run (`fb2e1eee`, 05:25). That earlier run made no tool calls, so it isn't a confirmed baseline.

**Hypotheses (unconfirmed)**

The client's declared tools changed at the same moment (table above): after the resume, the request itself lists tools named `mcp__magpie__Bash`, `mcp__magpie__Glob`, and so on. That leaves two readings:

1. **The bridge is returning the client's own declared name.** If the client sends a tool literally named `mcp__magpie__Bash`, handing a call back under that name is consistent. The question then becomes why the client's tool list switched from `Bash` to `mcp__magpie__Bash` at the resume, while its `magpie` server (the hub) doesn't actually offer those tools.
2. **The prefix-stripping rule misfires.** The client's hub is itself named `magpie`, so its tools (`mcp__magpie__context7__query-docs`, …) already start with `mcp__magpie__`. Per #4854, `bridgeToolName` special-cases names that already start with `mcp__magpie__` so they don't get a second prefix. Since #958, a resumed run's transcript also writes every past call as `mcp__magpie__PowerShell`. If those names get counted as the client's own on the resume path, the bridge would hand them over without stripping the prefix.

Either way, a long-lived run never goes through the resume path, which fits the failure starting only after it.

**Tried, didn't help:** switching to another Claude Code model with `/model`, and `/cd` to an existing folder (which failed with "session couldn't be moved").

**Workaround:** start a new client session instead of resuming.

**Can attach (redacted):** per-turn summaries and declared tool names for both gateway conversations, the app.log section above, the `api-request-shape` tool lists, and the 20 failed calls with their inputs and errors.

_Edited: corrected the error count (the earlier "9" counted mentions of the error in the model's replies, not failed calls) and added the client's declared tool names, which changed the hypothesis._
